data.body:
_More from Khopkar · Topical antifungals_

**Class:** Compound benzoic acid ointment (benzoic acid 6% + salicylic acid 3% in emulsifying base)

## Mechanism of action
- Benzoic acid: fungistatic; salicylic acid: keratolytic → sheds infected scale

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Tinea pedis (moccasin type), tinea corporis, tinea manuum, pityriasis versicolor — cheap, traditional ('half-strength' for children)

## Dose & formulations
- Twice daily for several weeks (until 2 weeks after clearance)

## Adverse effects
- Irritation, peeling, burning (especially on inflamed/fissured skin)

## Contraindications
- Acute inflamed skin, face, flexures (too irritating), large areas in children

## Pregnancy & lactation
Safe (small areas).

## Viva points
- Benzoic 6% + salicylic 3% — classic traditional antifungal

_Sources: Khopkar ch.19 (Traditional antifungal remedies). Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
